novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanistic investigation in the LLM setting—“a decodable ‘leading-hypothesis’ representation forms after the first few symptoms” and “under-updates when later disambiguating symptoms arrive”—rather than merely renaming an order effect; its novelty route is primarily a new mechanism and measurement applied to content-identical clinical symptom permutations. The closest prior work found was “Cognitive mechanisms underlying anchoring bias in diagnosis” (2026), which varies the position of salient distracting features in human clinical vignettes, alongside “Confirmatory information seeking is robust in psychologists’ diagnostic reasoning” (2024); searches used “LLM symptom order anchoring diagnosis,” “content-identical symptom order language model diagnosis,” “leading hypothesis representation activation patching,” “premature commitment reasoning LLM,” and “anchoring bias clinical diagnosis language models.” Moving from those studies to this claim is a natural extension on the phenomenon axis, but the proposed early representation, under-updating relationship, causal patching, and reset form a non-trivial mechanistic integration beyond a direct transfer; because the intervention and measurements rely on standard probing, steering, and activation patching rather than a new general-purpose paradigm, this supports standard-to-upper-standard novelty rather than high novelty.
